overview: S3 upload events go to a queue that triggers serverless functions: one splits the file, a fan-out of functions encodes chunks, a final step stitches manifests. Metadata lives in DynamoDB. Delivery via CDN with signed URLs.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative playback: 1M simultaneous viewers at 3 Mbps.
estimation.result: Playback traffic greatly exceeds small metadata/API responses.
estimation.implication: CDN absorbs segment traffic; scale transcoders by queue age and processing time, not viewer count.

entityDetails.purpose: Video processing state and published rendition manifest.
accessPatterns: Create upload; mark one processing version ready; read metadata for playback.
constraints: Publish READY only after all required segments and manifests exist.
relationships: MediaObject.video_id/processing_version identify objects referenced by the published manifest.

entityDetails.purpose: Immutable original bytes and generated media artifacts.
accessPatterns: Multipart upload raw bytes; workers read originals; CDN reads published segments.
constraints: Pin a processing version so an old retry cannot overwrite a newer manifest.
relationships: Video metadata selects a complete processing version; unreferenced outputs can be collected.

apiDetails.rationale: API returns signed upload parts; the creator sends media bytes to raw object storage.

apiDetails.purpose: Finalize the upload and schedule transcoding.
apiDetails.rationale: Use an outbox/object-store event and dedup processing version; duplicate completion must not publish incomplete media.

apiDetails.purpose: Retrieve playback metadata for a ready video.
apiDetails.rationale: The player fetches HLS/DASH segments from CDN and switches bitrate adaptively.

steps.title: Clients → API Gateway → Video Service → Video metadata
steps.explanation: Create resumable upload metadata and signed part URLs.

steps.title: Uploads bucket → Upload events → Encode functions → Encoded bucket
steps.explanation: Object events trigger idempotent chunk encoders; a completion barrier publishes the final manifest.

steps.title: Encode functions → Video metadata
steps.explanation: Conditionally mark the processing version READY.

steps.title: Clients → API Gateway → Video Service → Video metadata
steps.explanation: Read the latest complete manifest metadata.

steps.title: Clients → CDN → Encoded bucket
steps.explanation: Fetch DASH/HLS media segments via CDN; partial new outputs remain unpublished.

failureCases.scenario: A transcoder fails after writing some renditions
failureCases.handling: Retry deterministic versioned segment jobs, validate outputs and publish the manifest atomically when complete. Garbage-collect abandoned versions; the old READY version remains playable.

alternatives: Use worker transcoders for long jobs and GPU/codec control. Use event-triggered functions for bounded chunk jobs that fit runtime constraints, with an explicit completion barrier before publication.
